- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias in second half of forecast window.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward — increase forecast slightly to capture momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to reflect recent low as baseline.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67), model often averages out — use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
